                     1            Plaintiff Together AI, Inc., d/b/a Together Computer, Inc. (“Together”), for its Complaint

                     2   against Defendants Sesterce France Labs SAS (“Sesterce France Labs”), Sesterce Group SAS

                     3   (“Sesterce Group”) (collectively with Sesterce France Labs, “Sesterce” or “Defendants”), alleges

                     4   as follows:

                     5                                    PRELIMINARY STATEMENT

                     6            1.      Sesterce, a French technology business, entered into a business contract with

                     7   Together, a pioneering artificial intelligence company, and committed wrongdoings at every stage

                     8   of the parties’ dealings: Sesterce made key misrepresentations in negotiating the contract, later

                     9   attempted to finagle its way out of the contract, and eventually breached the contract. Together

                 10      seeks to hold Sesterce accountable for its wrongful actions and recover the tens of millions in

                 11      losses Together has suffered as a result of Sesterce’s deception and failure to keep its end of the

                 12      deal.

                 13               2.      In August 2024, Together entered into negotiations with Sesterce through its agent,

                 14      broker Hydra Host, Inc. (“Hydra”), regarding access to Together’s state-of-the-art cloud platform

                 15      called Together Forge (“Forge”). The platform helps businesses create and run custom generative

                 16      AI models. Sesterce specifically sought to access a number of “clusters” of Graphics Processing

                 17      Units (“GPUs”), which supply computing power that enables a user to train and run custom AI

                 18      tools—with the Forge platform enabling access to and use of the contracted-for clusters.

                 19               3.      On September 12, 2024, the parties executed a contract (the “Contract”) under

                 20      which Together agreed to provide Sesterce access to the Forge platform, including a specific

                 21      number of clusters, in exchange for monthly payments over a ten-month term, collectively totaling

                 22      approximately $20.6 million.1 The Contract identified Sesterce as the “customer” and was signed

                 23      by Sesterce’s CEO, Youssef El Manssouri; identified Hydra as the “broker” and was signed

                 24      Hydra’s CEO, Aaron Ginn; and identified Together as the “vendor” and was signed by Together’s

                 25      CEO, Vipul Ved Prakash.

                 26

                 27

                 28      1
                             The Contract is attached hereto as Exhibit A.

                     1          4.      Although Sesterce contracted with Together to obtain access to Forge, Sesterce

                     2   itself did not actually intend to use Forge. Instead, Sesterce needed Together’s platform and

                     3   services to support Sesterce’s own, independent customer (referred to as the “designated end user”

                     4   in the Contract)—Mistral AI, a French startup company that sought cloud computing power and

                     5   an AI training platform like Forge. While the Contract was in no way conditioned on the existence

                     6   of an “end user”—Sesterce was unconditionally liable for payment, no matter who actually used

                     7   the services Together agreed to provide—Together had sought assurances during the Contract

                     8   negotiations that Sesterce had in fact contracted with Mistral to be the end user of Forge for the

                     9   duration of the Contract term. The representations Together received regarding the existence of

                 10      such an agreement between Sesterce and Mistral for use of the Forge platform appeared to reduce

                 11      the amount of risk to Together, as Sesterce seemed to have the funds needed to fulfill its contractual

                 12      obligations. Sesterce, through its agent Hydra, had assured Together that Sesterce already had a

                 13      contract with Mistral that would run for at least the next ten months as of September 19, 2024,

                 14      when the parties executed the Contract.

                 15             5.      Performance under the Contract began without issue: Sesterce paid its first required

                 16      installment, and Mistral—as the end user—began using Forge within the parameters of the

                 17      Contract.

                 18             6.      Upon information and belief, and unbeknownst to Together, whatever agreement

                 19      (if any) Sesterce had with Mistral had expired by the time Sesterce and Together executed the

                 20      Contract. On November 4, 2024, nearly two months into the Contract, Sesterce came clean and

                 21      admitted to Together that, contrary to all representations made throughout the entire course of the

                 22      negotiations, Sesterce was in fact attempting to secure a new contract with Mistral. Although the

                 23      existence of a “designated end user” had no effect on the Contract or Sesterce’s obligation to pay

                 24      for the full term of Together’s services, for the next month Sesterce continued to offer Together

                 25      assurances about its relationship with Mistral, and by extension, Sesterce’s ability to perform under

                 26      the Contract. Indeed, Sesterce went out of its way to repeatedly tell Together that an agreement

                 27      between Sesterce and Mistral was imminent. Despite these repeated assurances, on December 3,

                 28      2024, Sesterce informed Together that Mistral had terminated negotiations with Sesterce.

                     1          7.      Rather than honor its contractual obligations, on December 31, 2024, Sesterce

                     2   purported to “rescind[]” the Contract on the pretense that Together had misled Sesterce during the

                     3   Contract negotiations. Specifically, Sesterce falsely asserted that Together had represented it

                     4   owned the computing equipment—the GPU clusters—that would be used under the Contract,

                     5   when in fact, Together had never hidden the fact that the number of clusters Sesterce requested

                     6   during the Contract negotiations would require Together to lease additional clusters from a third-

                     7   party. Beyond the patent falsity of Sesterce’s claim, ownership of the clusters was of no import:

                     8   the Contract is silent as to ownership of the clusters. Indeed, it is industry standard for computing

                     9   infrastructure to be leased, and contracts seldom, if ever, specify or require ownership of such

                 10      infrastructure. No wonder, then, that Sesterce never once inquired about ownership of the clusters

                 11      until December 31, 2024, after nearly a month of trying to find a means to escape its obligations

                 12      under the Contract.

                 13             8.      Together’s fears about Sesterce’s performance absent an end user—the very reason

                 14      Together had sought assurances that Sesterce had a formal agreement in place with Mistral to begin

                 15      with—were realized. Sesterce’s actions have caused and continue to cause Together substantial

                 16      damage.     Together thus brings this action to hold Sesterce accountable for its contractual

                 17      commitments, and to recover compensatory and punitive damages for Sesterce’s bad-faith and

                 18      unfair dealings with Together, in addition to interest, fees, and costs.

                     1                                            THE PARTIES

                     2          9.      Plaintiff Together AI, Inc. is a technology company that enables researchers,

                     3   developers, and businesses to develop, train, and deploy generative AI models. Together is

                     4   incorporated in Delaware, and its principal place of business is located at 251 Rhode Island

                     5   Street #205, San Francisco, California 94103.

                     6          10.     Together offers a suite of products, made available through its cloud platform

                     7   Forge, that enable users to develop open-source and custom AI models at low cost and with

                     8   industry-leading flexibility and efficiency. For example, Together offers “serverless inference,” a

                     9   cloud computing model that allows customers to deploy machine learning models without

                 10      managing the underlying computing infrastructure.          Together supports a diverse array of

                 11      customers, including nonprofits, small startups, established brands, and multi-billion-dollar

                 12      companies.

                 13             11.     Upon information and belief, Defendant Sesterce France Labs (SIRET

                 15      principal place of business at 50 Avenue des Caillols 13012, Marseille, France. Sesterce France

                 17      shell entity. Sesterce France Labs is the sole operational Sesterce entity, with all other affiliated

                 18      entities serving as shell or holding companies. Youssef El Manssouri is the CEO of Sesterce

                 19      France Labs.

                 20             12.     Upon information and belief, Defendant Sesterce Group SAS (SIRET

                 21      no. 90237248100025) is a corporation organized and existing under the laws of France with its

                 22      principal place of business at 50 Avenue des Caillols 13012, Marseille, France. Sesterce Group is

                 23      the holding company of Sesterce France Labs, with no employees or business operations of its

                 24      own.

                 27      is complete diversity between the Plaintiff (a citizen of California and Delaware) and Defendants

                 28      (citizens of France), and the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000.

                     3   Defendants entered a business relationship with Together—a California-based company whose

                     4   employees primarily work and reside in California—to receive access to Together’s computing

                     5   tools and services, and this dispute arises directly from that business relationship.

                     6          15.     This Court is the proper venue for this Complaint pursuant to 28 U.S.C.

                     7   § 1391(b)(2) because a substantial part of the events giving rise to the claims occurred in this

                     8   judicial district. Together accepted and executed the Contract in San Francisco, where it is

                     9   headquartered; the Contract’s obligations and liabilities arise in California; Defendants, through

                 10      broker Hydra, wired a down payment of $1.7 million to Together’s bank account in California;

                 11      and Defendants’ breach caused Together to suffer harm in California.

                     3          30.      Based on these discussions, Together understood that Sesterce had ten months

                     4   remaining on a contract with Mistral, and that Mistral was the end user who would ultimately be

                     5   using Forge.      Having never previously engaged with Sesterce, and without financial

                     6   documentation proving Sesterce’s independent ability to pay for Together’s services, this

                     7   assurance—that Mistral, a known and reputable company, would be contractually bound (for at

                     8   least ten months) to pay Sesterce for Mistral’s use of Forge—alleviated Together’s concerns about

                     9   Sesterce’s ability to perform under the Contract, which in turn put Together at ease about moving

                 11             31.      The truth, however, as Together later learned, was that at the time of the Contract

                 12      negotiations in September 2024, whatever service contract Sesterce had with Mistral—if any—

                 13      would expire that autumn. In fact, unbeknownst to Together, Sesterce was attempting to secure

                 14      Mistral’s business for an additional undisclosed term by having obtained from Together a high-

                 16             32.      Another key topic addressed during the negotiations was the Contract’s duration.

                 17      Sesterce initially wanted to enter a ten-month contract with Together, which further confirmed to

                 18      Together that Sesterce had ten months remaining on its purported service contract with Mistral.

                 19      Together Representative, however, urged that the Contract between Together and Sesterce be for

                 20      twelve months. Together Representative explained that Together could not enter a contract term

                 21      of less than twelve months for a cluster of this size. Sesterce expressed no concern about the

                 22      ownership of the node cluster during negotiations of the Contract. Together then entered into a

                 23      lease of the necessary GPUs with a third-party vendor (detailed infra ¶ 37).

                 24             33.      The parties ultimately agreed to a 304-day term (approximately ten months), with

                 25      the Contract automatically renewing for one year upon its expiration unless Sesterce provided at

                 26      least sixty days’ notice before the end of the initial term to opt out of auto-renewal. Together

                 27      agreed to a ten-month term, believing, based on Sesterce and Hydra’s repeated and unwavering

                 28      representations, that Sesterce had ten months remaining on its service contract with Mistral.

                     1          34.     On September 10, 2024, Together gave Sesterce access to the cluster to test and set

                     2   up a channel on Together’s communications platform, Slack, to support testing.

                     3          35.     By September 12, 2024, Together and Hydra—on behalf of Sesterce—had settled

                     4   on the substantive terms of the Contract, agreeing to language that obligated Sesterce to pay

                     5   Together all monies due on the Contract.

                     6          36.     On or about September 19, 2024, Together’s CEO signed the Contract on behalf of

                     7   Together, and Sesterce and Hydra signed thereafter. The Contract identifies Sesterce as the

                     8   “customer,” Hydra as the “broker,” and Together as the “vendor.”

                     9          37.     The Contract requires Together to provide Sesterce and its end user with “access to

                 10      at least 80 nodes” with at least “90% availability” over the Contract’s first two months. In

                 11      providing access to its Forge training platform under the Contract, Together had significant cost

                 12      outlays, including the cost of GPUs, a physical asset through which the digital software operates.

                 13      To satisfy its obligations under the Contract, Together leased GPU access for twenty-four months

                 14      from a third-party vendor, at a total cost of $36,419,174.40, of which $16,209,587.20 came from

                 15      the ten months covered by the Contract.

                 16             38.     In exchange for access to Together Forge, the Contract requires Sesterce to make

                 17      twelve payments to Together totaling $20,569,882 over the course of roughly eleven months: an

                 18      initial payment upon execution of the contract for $1,711,821; another payment in the same
